findings.location: source.html and translation.html: /article[1]/p[18], p[20] (two quotations), p[21], p[27]
findings.source_quote: The article quotes Scripture at Mar 9:47, 1Pe 3:4-5, Mat 18:7, Jas 3:13, and Tit 2:12. scripture_evidence identifies no quotes, and scripture_selections is empty.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide the required approved target-language Scripture evidence for each quoted passage and replace each translated quotation with the precisely corresponding target-verse text, preserving the source ellipses, quotation boundaries, references, and placement. Then supply one audited scripture_selections item per quotation. Do not generate substitute Scripture wording without evidence.
findings.translation_quote: Examples include “ni afadhali kwako kuingia katika ufalme wa Mungu…” (p[18]), “Lakini uzuri wenu uwe utu wa moyoni…” and “…ole wake yule…” (p[20]), and the quotations at p[21] and p[27].

findings.source_quote: “Would you let your girls use them?”
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the malformed word to: “Ungew ruhusu” is also not standard; use “Ungew aruhusu” only if referring to the girls. Prefer: “Ungew aruhusu binti zako wazitumie?”

findings.source_quote: I wonder if I’ve changed, or if the times have changed, or what.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the apparent typo to “nimebadilika”: “Naishia kujiuliza kama ni mimi niliye badilika, au nyakati zimebadilika, au nini.”
findings.translation_quote: “Naishia kujiuliza kama ni mimi niliye muuttika, au nyakati zimebadilika, au nini.”

findings.source_quote: the surrendering sigh of a mother unable to pass her principles on to her teenage daughters
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the unclear “sigha” with a natural Kiswahili rendering, for example: “kuugua kwa mama anayejisalimisha kwa kushindwa kuwafundisha binti zake matineja kanuni zake.”
findings.translation_quote: “sigha ya mama anayekubali kushindwa, asiyeweza kuwafundisha binti zake matineja kanuni zake”
